doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

chapter: Army, Chicago and the new music
title: Army in Heidelberg and Muhal's big band rehearsals
summary: In the Army in Heidelberg he met Karl Berger, Albert Mangelsdorff, Bent Jaedig and Nathaniel Davis at sessions; he then describes Muhal's big band at the C & C Lounge where members wrote for the band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Absolutely. He’s totally right on that. You know. Totally right. But I go way back with Karl Berger. When I was in the Army in Heidelberg, Germany, there was a K-54 and Karl Berger was down there with the musicians down there — Albert Mangelsdorff was there, Bent Jaedig, the great tenor saxophonist from Denmark, and you know Nathaniel Davis, his quartet had won the All-Army championship or whatever, so they came to live with us in Heidelberg. So I used to hang out with him and go down there and there would always be these sessions and so on and so forth. So yeah, yeah I mean to me I’m glad to be a part of the people that have had the chance to have long term musical relationships. Because there’s no way in the world, you know, you can develop this kind of work, you know, without doing that. When we were all in Chicago there, you know we had an agenda, you know, we knew that like we were going to go to the C & C Lounge for the rehearsals with Muhal’s Big Band and he would encourage all the musicians in the band to write for the band. And so you’d write for the band and you’d bring your music in to hear it. If he didn’t like it you could take it home and change it and so on and so forth. So it always has to be placed in that context. Because a lot of times you might know something but you may not know it at that moment so you may have to just keep working until it starts to reveal itself to you. So, and once that happens then you’ve got a helper.
